key_insight: This cardiac imaging study—not cancer drug discovery—uses personalised healthy digital twins to reveal heart-shape and motion deviations associated with cardiovascular risk beyond conventional biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: Deviation scores may improve risk stratification in people with preserved ejection fraction, but predictive signals differed between cardiac representations.
method: Generate expected healthy cardiac function matched to age, sex and body habitus.
Measure individual deviations using statistical shape models and a generative mesh autoencoder.
Test added risk-prediction value beyond conventional cardiac biomarkers, with cross-validation and Gaussian-noise controls.
evidence_signal: In two UK Biobank cohorts (HeartSSM n=52,365; MeshHeart n≤39,376), preserved-EF analyses showed improved discrimination for atrial fibrillation with HeartSSM (ΔC=0.068; cross-validated ΔC=0.063) and stroke with MeshHeart (ΔC=0.024), which showed no atrial-fibrillation signal.
watch_item: External testing involved 315 healthy volunteers rather than outcome validation; clinical utility and transportability of risk predictions remain unestablished.
paper_title: Personalised normative cardiac phenotyping reveals clinically relevant heterogeneity in cardiac shape and outcome risk
